headline: Mistakes to Avoid When Planning a Home Kitchen Expansion
articleBody:
Expanding your kitchen creates wonderful living space, but jumping ahead without thorough planning can lead to expensive setbacks. Here are common pitfalls to avoid before construction begins:

1. Starting Demolition Before Permits Are Issued: Beginning framing or teardown before your building department grants approvals risks stop-work orders and fines. Ensure your builder pulls all required structural, plumbing, and electrical permits first.
2. Underestimating Utility Demands: Adding new ovens, dishwashers, and ventilation hoods requires serious electrical and gas service. Failing to verify service capacity early can stall progress when lines must be upgraded.
3. Choosing Cabinets Before Confirming Wall Dimensions: Ordering cabinetry based on preliminary sketches rather than verified rough-in framing leads to costly delays. Always confirm final measurements after framing is complete.
4. Overlooking Structural Load Paths: Cutting into exterior or interior walls without calculating load distribution can cause structural sagging. Have a qualified contractor verify load-bearing headers and foundation tie-ins.
5. Forgetting Temporary Kitchen Logistics: Construction takes weeks. Failing to set up a clean temporary prep area with a microwave and refrigerator makes daily life chaotic during major work.
